correctness.rationale: The subtree feasible interval recurrence is proved by the integer adjacency of windows [s-delta_c(s),s] indexed by consecutive child times. Independently conditioned child subtrees yield the exact Bellman max-sum equation; a sorted endpoint max-heap sweep and range-add difference arrays evaluate every message in O(S log S). A standalone verifier matches an independently enumerated optimum and witness for 5750 randomly generated finite trees and checks a strict confluence obstruction. The induction, not tests, proves the infinite-family claim. Assumptions include explicit time-value input, nonnegative admissible horizons and one fixed parent per nonroot voter.

value.rationale: Time-consciousness and confluence are the two central desiderata of the source voting framework, whose combination with utility optimization is hard generally. A fixed referral hierarchy with stable uninterrupted approval is a motivated organizational restriction; the result supplies the exact remaining eligibility of every subtree and a near-linear utility-optimal assignment despite arbitrary changes in trust horizons, plus a small example explaining why local path checks alone are inadequate. The improvement is not a mere numeric constant and the full nonmonotone input family is natural.
